content:
For years, collectors have had a fondness for Steve Jobs memorabilia, and a new lot is expected to generate tremendous interest. It is Jobs' 8th-grade science fair project, which includes two demonstration circuits and a warning note he wrote to his teacher.

The project has been kept at the Jobs family property in Los Altos, but is now one of more than 200 lots in an Apple 50th anniversary auction...

Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and RR Auctions is holding a two-part auction for the occasion, called "Steve Jobs and the Computer Revolution: Apple 50th Anniversary Auction." In the first part of the auction, the company's first check written went for as much as $2.4 million.

The second part includes the aforementioned science fair project.

The warning note likely reflects the risk of the circuits burning out if left running for a long time. As of writing, the online bid was below $3,000, but the price is expected to rise significantly.

Among the lots is also a fully functional early Apple 1.

As well as a development prototype of the original iPod.
